source_text: Dicunt etiam istas quae modo aguntur nuptias a Deo institutas non fuisse, quod in libro Augustini legitur, contra quem ego modo quattuor libellis respondi
pass_a_gloss: They also say that these marriages which are now being carried on were not instituted by God, which is read in Augustine's book, against which I have now answered in four little books.

lemmas.lexica: LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: They also say that the marriages now taking place were not instituted by God. This can be read in Augustine’s book, which I have just answered in four short books.

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, De nuptiis et concupiscentia 2 / On Marriage and Concupiscence); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
